title: The Spring That Never Learned Its Own Source

features.name: the cycling water
features.desc-on-touch: You trace the spring upward, but the water beneath your fingers moves only in circles. No source, only the shape of returning. The spring forgets where it came from each time it surfaces.

features.name: the unnamed tributary
features.desc-on-touch: Water enters from the dark without a name. No map has ever called it anything. The trees above remember it as only a sound.

features.name: the listening moss
features.desc-on-touch: Green grows thick here where the spring learns to be quiet. The moss holds the sound of water forgetting its own name. Damp, old, patient. You could read the strata if you had the time the moss has.

features.name: the water's mirror
features.desc-on-touch: The spring holds a surface that reflects but refuses to remember what it reflects. Each image is born and dies in the same instant. The water shows you but never keeps the picture.

features.name: the depth below
features.desc-on-touch: You look down into water and the water looks back up at you. It's the same look. The spring has no bottom, or its bottom is the same as its surface, or the distinction has never mattered here.

inscription: the water comes back but never to the place it left

file.name: SpringSource_Hydrology_1987.txt
file.note: Survey attempts to trace the spring's origin, but each vector collapses into the spring itself. The file now loops on itself, returning without arriving.

reverie.title: REVERIE — by the circular water at dusk
narr: You both stand thigh-deep, the water between warm and cold.
She asks where the spring comes from and you admit you've never
found the start. She nods like she already knew the answer. The
light at the treeline holds the colour of leaving. Her hands are
steady on the stones. No one needs to know the story of water.
